note: The line renderer (register decisions 278-286). Judged two ways: the CPU half, view/LineBatch, by test_line_batch; the GPU half -- the renderer, the probe, the line shaders, the device and pipeline requirements -- by the lines probe's CTest tests, the number check test_probe_lines and the port check. The flush VulkanContext::writeMapped performs is M1-107's mutant, merged there (owner's ruling, 2026-10-04), and not repeated here.

mutants.why: The probe draws with a white tint, so a shader that ignores the tint draws the same frame: equivalent here. Predicted before the pass and confirmed by it; accepted by the owner, 2026-10-04 (register decision 318), to be killed by the first caller that uses a tint other than white.

the port check holds on lines' picture, to 1/255 and to 2/65535
mutants.why: No line of the lines probe passes behind another: the three axes meet only at the origin, where they share one depth, so writing depth changes no pixel. Depth writes matter once lines are drawn over a surface -- the reason the task gives for switching them off -- so the first task that draws lines over a surface, the orbit track over the Earth (M1-76), kills it. Accepted by the owner, 2026-10-04 (register decision 317).

mutants.why: Measured 2026-10-04 on the RX 7900 XTX, driver 26.8.1: the device is created without the extension but with its bresenhamLines feature in the chain, the driver -- a Vulkan 1.4 implementation, where line rasterization is core -- honours it, and validation layers 1.4.363 report nothing, so the probe draws the same frame. vk-bootstrap enables only the extensions it is asked for, read in its source. The request stays: Vulkan 1.3, which this renderer targets, requires it. A known gap accepted by the owner (register decision 316); the mutant below, which drops both requests, is caught.

The survivor was accepted by the owner in advance, 2026-10-04 (question 5 of M1-19), with the A2000's golden named as what catches it there (decision 306); the phase A gate saw it caught there, 2026-10-07, and gave the verdict per card (decisions 410 and 411).
